text: Basho: no manual way to set now
Basho: the now tracker jumped backward or refused to advance
Basho: the place details page was hard to reach and to leave
Basho: poor in cities: backtracking and several similar routes to one place
Basho: route data showed unconnected lanes as connected
Basho: maps were incomplete and did not mirror OSM roads and trails
Basho: road size was unclear at a glance
Basho: no one-tap bug report capturing screenshot and state
Basho: no trip-wide list of shopping options; stores were buried in footnotes
Basho: no list of meal options in a place; an unexpected closure left no fallback
Basho: maps had no key or legend
Basho: routes gave no reason for their choice of way
Basho: battery drain despite being offline and mostly static
Basho: static and computed times looked the same, so every listed time was confusing
Basho: no overview map of the day's arc, only leg by leg
Basho: train legs lacked platform and headsign; the wrong train was taken once
Basho: overnight towns had no evening page (dinner, night activities, practical items)
Basho: sights in a town could not be seen relative to each other and to the legs
CI and test speed was a huge blocker; the suite was huge, bloated and unoptimized
Much of the test suite enforced what should have been compile-time or type-level facts
The full suite ran on unrelated changes; a small data change forced a full rebuild and recheck
App code and trip data were not separated (not a general travel app taking data files)
Nobody knew which code affected which features, so everything was rechecked and CI ran out
Development was serial: the current feature blocked unrelated work (worst with #72)
Criticality was haphazard and miscalibrated in both directions, with no triage across the spec
Tracking implemented versus unimplemented features was a mess
Worktrees did not share a compiler cache or build directory
Simulators were shared instead of one per agent or test group
Flaky tests were retried and forgotten instead of flagged and fixed
The UI check used a browser for facts that need no layout, and for untouched screens
Data was keyed by leg numbers, not stable ids; generated files were large and coarse
Most time was spent waiting for CI and tests
The main session relayed every hand-off while agents sat idle
No single source of truth: status files, a handoff note and the main session's context
Agents collided on simulators, Chrome, search quota and data files
Ownership of work was unclear
Work died with the session or the laptop
Exists plus green CI was taken to mean correct
How data was verified (simulator, user, online sources) was tribal knowledge, not typed
The spec was not encoded; the code was its own definition of done
Manual steps (simulator runs, Playwright lookups) were never proceduralized and left no trail
Tests that cannot fail were counted as evidence
Performance profiles and optimisation effort were not recorded
Push after every commit was a written rule; the overnight fixer pushed only once at the end
The owner reviews and merges every PR, a bottleneck that worsens as agents parallelise; goal: most PRs merged sight-unseen, with merge authority earned per risk tier
Stage 0: meta/log, minimal schema, meta CLI, hooks, seed. Exit test: one week of meta-development's own work run from the log, no hand-written handoff notes
Prerequisite for stage 1: cloud CI (fix GitHub billing or choose another runner)

Stage 1: runs and timing for every check; failing wall-time budgets; flaky reruns recorded with a flakiness budget; complexity and vagueness budgets as counts. Exit test: a budget has actually blocked something
Onboard Basho as the test subject right after stage 0/1, through its own meta.toml only
Stage 2: meta run trail recorder; first procedure (Playwright lookup); researcher and tester roles. Exit test: two agents run the same procedure and get comparable, inspectable trails

Stage 3: typed subjects, properties, claims; evidence kinds; ladder typestate; severity budget; done needs evidence; evidence check in CI. Exit test: meta-development's own features show computed status and confidence
